Positive-part convexity, monotonicity on nonnegative functions and Minkowski give convexity including d=1. Dropping (x−1)_+^D gives the bound for g(x−1), also for 0≤x<1.

For q>1, 0<p=1/(d+1)<1 and the first term of h is strictly concave on the closed interval; the second is concave and continuous up to its zero argument. The initial derivative is positive. At the other endpoint, 1+((q+1)/q)^d<1+2^d<2^(d+1). Strict concavity gives strict decrease of h(s)/s for s>0 and continuity gives one interior zero. Reciprocation reverses the sign regions, giving E_q(F)≤0 exactly on [q^d,B(q)].

At the barrier the root triple is U−δ,U,U+δ with U−δ>0. Raising successive positive D-power differences to 1/d gives q and q+1 after scaling by δ^(D/d). Convexity bounds the next increment below by q+2 in this scale. Hence E_(q+1)(G)≤0 at G=B(q)+(q+1)^d, in its valid domain, and the next barrier lies at or above G.

At the first triple the left increment comparison uses δ^(D/d)g(t−1)≤δ^(D/d)t^(D/d)=ρ, without assuming t≥1. This gives A_2^p+A_0^p≤2A_1^p and A_1≤B(ρ+1). The inductive addition of the next power is exact, with A_m≥(ρ+m)^d at every tested index.

For noninteger q>1, ρ is the fractional part and m=floor(q)≥1. For integer q≥2, ρ=1 and m=q−1≥1. In each case the same ρ and m+j identify the sums at q+j for j=−1,0,1, including the smallest q and zero endpoint terms.

At ρ=1 the upper Riemann sum of t^d on unit intervals dominates its integral, giving A_m≥(m+1)^(d+1)/(d+1). If α>1/(d+1), A_m^α/(m+1) is unbounded, contradicting the affine upper bound from nonincreasing first differences. The integer q=m+1 identification transfers this failure.
